True Color.description: Natural-color imagery from NASA satellites, showing Earth as the human eye would see it. Ideal for visual storytelling and general context.

layers.name: True Color — Current
layers.subtitle: VIIRS NOAA-21
layers.description: Default base map. Most current-generation daily true color, 375m. Use for 'what does it look like today/recently'.
layers.gibsDescription:
True Color: Red = Band I1, Green = Band M4, Blue = Band M3

These images are called true-color or natural color because this combination of wavelengths is similar to what the human eye would see. The images are natural-looking images of land surface, oceanic and atmospheric features.

The Visible Infrared Imaging Radiometer Suite (VIIRS) Corrected Reflectance imagery is available only as near real-time imagery. The VIIRS instrument is aboard the joint NASA/NOAA NOAA-21 (JPSS-2) satellite. The imagery can be visualized in Worldview and the Global Imagery Browse Services (GIBS). The sensor resolution is 750 m and 375 m (M Bands are 750 m, I Bands are 375 m), imagery resolution is 250 m, and the temporal resolution is daily.

Note: The Corrected Reflectance and the Thermal Band I5 imagery from NOAA-21/VIIRS will occasionally show a checkered pattern, especially over the respective polar areas. This is due to overlapping and superimposition of observations from multiple orbits with widely different cloud/snow coverages. The checkered pattern may also arise from the mixture of partial day and night observations. Though all necessary steps have been taken to mitigate this effect, users may still notice this to some extent over the polar areas, depending on the season.

layers.name: True Color — Long Record
layers.description: Only true-color option with a record back to 2000. Use for multi-year/decade before-after comparisons, not day-to-day snapshots.
layers.gibsDescription:
MODIS Corrected Reflectance vs. MODIS Surface Reflectance

The MODIS Corrected Reflectance algorithm utilizes MODIS Level 1B data (the calibrated, geolocated radiances). It is not a standard, science quality product. The purpose of this algorithm is to provide natural-looking images by removing gross atmospheric effects, such as Rayleigh scattering, from MODIS visible bands 1-7. The algorithm was developed by the original MODIS Rapid Response team to address the needs of the fire monitoring community who want to see smoke. Corrected Reflectance shows smoke more clearly than the standard Surface Reflectance product. In contrast, the MODIS Land Surface Reflectance product (MOD09) is a more complete atmospheric correction algorithm that includes aerosol correction, and is designed to derive land surface properties. In clear atmospheric conditions the Corrected Reflectance product is very similar to the MOD09 product, but they depart from each other in presence of aerosols. If you wish to perform a complete atmospheric correction, please do not use the Corrected Reflectance algorithm. An additional difference is that the Land Surface Reflectance product is only tuned for calculating the reflectance over land surfaces.

References: NASA Earthdata - Creating Reprojected True Color MODIS Images: A Tutorial; NASA Earthdata Forum - LANCE FAQ

Precipitation.description: Rain and snowfall measurements from satellite sensors. Track storms, monsoons, and rainfall anomalies over time.

layers.name: Precipitation — Right Now
layers.description: Near-real-time global precipitation, 10km, updated every 30 min. The 'is it raining there today' layer. Use dates within the last few days.
layers.subtitle: IMERG NRT

layers.name: Precipitation — Historical Event
layers.description: IMERG archive for reconstructing a specific past storm. Needs a full ISO datetime. Example default set to Cyclone Freddy's Mozambique landfall.
layers.subtitle: IMERG Archive

Vegetation.description: Plant health and density indicators (NDVI, EVI). Monitor drought impact, crop health, and seasonal greenness changes.

layers.name: Vegetation — NDVI Trend
layers.description: Monthly NDVI composite, least cloud noise. Use for season-to-season or year-to-year comparison stories (crop stress, greening/browning trends).
layers.subtitle: MODIS Terra Monthly

layers.name: Vegetation — NDVI Current
layers.description: Current-generation 8-day NDVI composite. Use when the monthly layer is too stale for a fast-moving story.
layers.subtitle: VIIRS NOAA-20

Air Quality.description: Atmospheric composition data including aerosols, dust, smoke, and pollutant concentrations. Key for air quality reporting.

layers.name: Air Quality — NO₂
layers.description: Best-available NO2 column, ~7km, near-daily. Urban pollution, industrial emissions, biomass burning. Use for city air-quality stories.
layers.subtitle: TROPOMI Sentinel-5P

layers.name: Air Quality — Aerosols
layers.description: Combined aerosol optical depth, 10km. The Saharan dust / biomass-burning-smoke layer. Central for the Southern Africa burning-season and Sahara dust stories.
layers.subtitle: MODIS Combined AOD

layers.name: Air Quality — SO₂
layers.description: SO2 vertical column, ~7km, near-daily. Detects volcanic eruptions and industrial/power-plant emissions. Kept specifically for East African Rift volcano stories (e.g. Nyiragongo).
layers.subtitle: TROPOMI Sentinel-5P

Wildfire.description: Active fire detections, burn scars, and fire radiative power. Essential for wildfire monitoring and aftermath analysis.

layers.name: Active Fires — Current
layers.description: Flagship active-fire point layer, 375m, day+night. This is the headline wildfire layer.
layers.subtitle: VIIRS NOAA-20

layers.name: Active Fires — Extra Pass
layers.description: Same product family as NOAA-20, adds an extra daily overpass. Surface as a togglable variant under 'Active Fires', not a separate menu item.
layers.subtitle: VIIRS NOAA-21

layers.name: Active Fires — Extended
layers.description: Same product family, oldest VIIRS platform. Togglable variant under 'Active Fires' for maximum daily coverage.
layers.subtitle: VIIRS Suomi NPP

layers.name: Active Fires — Historical
layers.description: Coarser (1km) but the only fire-detection layer with a record back to the early 2000s. Use for 'is this worse than previous years' comparison stories.
layers.subtitle: MODIS Terra+Aqua

layers.name: Burn Scars — False Color
layers.description: 375m false color; burn scars appear orange-red. Use alongside the active-fire points to show cumulative damage, not just today's detections.
layers.subtitle: VIIRS M11-I2-I1

Floods.description: Surface water extent and flood detection imagery. Useful for disaster response and flood risk assessment.

layers.name: Flood Extent — MODIS 1-Day
layers.subtitle: MODIS Terra+Aqua
layers.description: MODIS Combined Flood 1-Day. Best-resolution flood extent from MODIS (since 2000). Use for historical African floods (e.g. 2022 Nigeria, Lake Chad, Sudd). NOTE: Gibson's default VIIRS flood layer only has data from ~2025 onward.

layers.name: Flood Extent — MODIS 3-Day
layers.subtitle: MODIS Terra+Aqua
layers.description: MODIS Combined Flood 3-Day composite. Averages 3 days to reduce cloud false-positives. Best for clean historical flood maps.

layers.name: Flood Extent — Current
layers.description: Best-resolution near-real-time flood extent. A frequent, distinct African story from precipitation — this is the 'impact' layer, IMERG is the 'cause' layer.
layers.subtitle: VIIRS 375m

Drought.description: Soil moisture, evaporation, and water stress indicators. Track drought conditions and water availability.

layers.name: Drought — Soil Moisture
layers.description: Surface (0-5cm) soil moisture, ~36km, daily. Responds fast to rainfall deficit — use this over the L4 root-zone product for single-season drought stories.
layers.subtitle: SMAP L3 Passive

layers.name: Drought — Land Temperature
layers.description: 1km daily daytime land surface temp. The heat-stress companion to soil moisture.
layers.subtitle: MODIS Terra LST

layers.name: Drought — Groundwater
layers.description: ~300km, monthly. Coarse, but the only satellite product that sees deep aquifer depletion. Kept specifically for basin-scale stories: Lake Chad, Nile/GERD.
layers.subtitle: GRACE-FO Mascon

base.name: Blue Marble — Static Reference
base.description: Static NASA Blue Marble reference imagery. Good fallback base when daily imagery is patchy; loads at Level8.
base.gibsDescription:
About Blue Marble

The MODIS Blue Marble, Next Generation is a static product created with data from 2004 from the MODIS instrument on board the Terra satellite. The image resolution is 500 m. It can be viewed in Worldview/Global Imagery Browse Services (GIBS). Images for January – December 2004 can be downloaded from NASA’s Visible Earth.

References: NASA Earth Observatory - Blue Marble; NASA Earth Observations - Blue Marble; NASA Earth Observations - Blue Marble: Next Generation+Topography and Bathymetry
base.subtitle: MODIS Terra

reference.name: Coastlines
reference.description: Static vector coastline reference overlay. Uses the GIBS 'default' time keyword, so it is date-independent and always available.
reference.gibsDescription:
The Coastlines layer is a reference layer that displays global coastlines.

Coastlines information are gleaned from OpenStreetMap and the SCAR Antarctic Digital Database (2010) for Antarctic coastlines.
reference.subtitle: Static overlay

reference.name: Place Labels
reference.description: Place and country labels (GIBS Reference_Labels, Level9). Static reference overlay.
reference.gibsDescription:
The Place Labels layer is a reference layer that displays labels for countries, states, major cities, minor cities, towns, airports, universities/schools, hospitals, water bodies, and national parks/protected areas.

Place Labels information are provided by Esri, TomTom, Garmin, FAO, NOAA, USGS, © OpenStreetMap contributors, and the GIS User Community via the Hybrid Reference Layer (WGS84).

Alignment of boundaries is a presentation of the feature provided by our data vendors and does not imply endorsement by Esri or any governing authority.
reference.subtitle: Cities & countries

reference.name: Reference Features
reference.description: Political border and feature lines (GIBS Reference_Features, Level9). Static reference overlay.
reference.gibsDescription:
The Coastlines/Borders/Roads layer is a reference layer that displays global coastlines, country borders, first order administrative boundaries and major roads.

Coastlines/Borders/Roads information are gleaned from OpenStreetMap and Natural Earth.
reference.subtitle: Borders & roads

reference.name: Graticule Grid
reference.description: Latitude/longitude graticule (GIBS Graticule_15m, Level13). Static reference overlay.
reference.gibsDescription:
The Latitude-Longitude Lines layer is a vector layer displaying the grid/graticule of latitude and longitude lines over the globe.

In the geographic projection, Latitude-Longitude Lines were generated from Shapefiles provided by Natural Earth. For the Arctic and Antarctic polar stereographic projections, the graticule layers were generated from Polarview.
reference.subtitle: Lat/lon lines

reference.name: Land Mask
reference.description: OpenStreetMap-derived land/ocean mask (GIBS OSM_Land_Mask, Level9). Darkens oceans as an underlay.
reference.gibsDescription:
The Land Mask overlay layer is a representation of land in dark grey. It was created as a way to mask land-covered areas to focus only on areas of water.

The Land/Water Map was gleaned from OpenStreetMap.
reference.subtitle: Ocean darkening

_notes.provenance: Restored full layer catalogue from layers-full-backup.json on 2026-08-04. Categories with icons replace the old flat sections structure. Context category (GPW Population Density) intentionally excluded. GIBS metadata preserved from the enriched layers.json.
_notes.timeFormat: Per-layer dates are intentionally NOT stored here — resolved at runtime (default for daily layers is yesterday). startDate/endDate reflect GIBS availability windows, shown in layer details.
_notes.fireGrouping: The three VIIRS active-fire layers share group: active_fires_viirs — render as one feature with a satellite-pass toggle, not three menu entries.
_notes.categories: Each category has an icon and description. Layers are grouped under the category's 'layers' array.
